standard_prerequisites.name: The functoriality of the module of differentials for a commutative diagram of sheaves of rings, with the map characterised on differentials of local sections
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Author lemma lemma-functoriality-differentials, whose statement is reproduced verbatim as a context span of this card (source lines 5136-5157)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the situation in which the statement is formulated and the right hand map of the sequence.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Leibniz rule for the universal derivation, and the compatibility of the formation of differentials with taking stalks
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof (source lines 5184-5191 and 5195-5197)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the displayed rule defines a map on the quotient by the square of the kernel and identifies the sequence with the algebraic one.

core_obligations: Well definedness: for local sections of the kernel the proof checks that the rule sending a class to the differential tensored with one annihilates products, which follows from the Leibniz rule (proof lines 5184-5191)
Linearity: a similar computation shows that the map so defined is linear over the quotient sheaf of rings (proof lines 5192-5193)
The second map: the map on the right is the functoriality map of the context lemma for the given diagram (proof lines 5193-5194)
Exactness: the sequence may be checked on stalks, where it becomes the corresponding algebraic sequence (proof lines 5195-5199)
proof_roadmap: 对局部截面 f ∈ I 记其像为 f̄；验证 f̄ ↦ df ⊗ 1 有定义只需 Leibniz 法则：d(f_1f_2) ⊗ 1 = (f_1 df_2 + f_2 df_1) ⊗ 1 = df_2 ⊗ f_1 + df_1 ⊗ f_2 = 0。
同样计算给出 O'_2 = O_2/I-线性；右端映射取 functoriality 引理给的那个；正合性可在茎上检验（lemma-abelian），于是化为交换代数的同一序列（跨章引理）。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement gives, for a surjection of sheaves of algebras over a common base, the canonical exact sequence relating the square of the kernel to the modules of differentials, with the left map characterised by sending a local section to its differential tensored with one (author lemma at source lines 5163-5181, label lemma-differential-seq). The proof (source lines 5183-5200) verifies well definedness and linearity by the Leibniz rule, identifies the right hand map with the functoriality map, and reduces exactness to stalks, where the algebraic sequence applies (proof lines 5184-5199). The Leibniz computation is the content; the situation of the statement is reproduced verbatim as a context span. H2.
